Subject: Greenline procurement: short-log exception & pilot steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a concrete path. I pulled together specifics below based on your questions and what the security/procurement teams asked for.

Summary of ask from Greenline:
- Short retention window for model inputs/KV (7 days preferred) for the clinical triage workload.
- No PII should be persisted in logs; any PII must be redacted prior to storage.
- Data residency: US-only for logs/evidence.
- Evidence for SOC 2 controls around logging and retention to satisfy procurement.

Redwood proposal (pilot scope):
- 7-day ephemeral log window applied to triage route only (isolated route config).
- Automatic PII-scrubbing step in the ingest pipeline (we showed a sample regex-based redactor on the call).
- Audit evidence: we will provide SOC2 summary, config snapshot, and an export of retention settings for audit.
- Pilot duration: 30 days, during which retention behavior is audited weekly and we’ll share an anonymized sample (redacted) of stored entries.

Requested from Greenline to move forward:
- Confirmation that a 7-day pilot is acceptable versus an immediate 0-retention requirement.
- Any procurement templates or MSAs you expect us to use for this pilot.
- A primary technical contact for configuring route-level policies.

Attachments: I’m attaching the pilot spec and a short SOC2 summary for your procurement team.

Next steps / mutual action plan:
1) Greenline confirms pilot scope and acceptable minimum retention (Samantha) — target: EOD Thu 4/9.
2) Redwood SE (Marissa) to share a route-level config and a short list of redaction rules — target: 48 hours after confirmation.
3) Legal to circulate pilot addendum (Ben/Neha) if procurement needs it — target: 3 business days after procurement template received.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up with your security folks if that helps.

Cheers,
Rachel

--

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the clear summary. Procurement and security had a quick sync and here's what they said:

- Procurement is generally open to a 7-day pilot but will want language that guarantees no escalation to longer retention without written consent.
- Security’s hard requirement is: zero PII at rest. If your redactor can be demonstrated in our environment (or on a mirrored dataset) before any data persists, that may satisfy them.
- We need logs to remain in US-only regions for the duration of the pilot.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can the redaction step run entirely in our VPC (private deployment) to avoid exfil risks? If not, can you document the flow and controls?
2) For the 7-day retention, will you expose automated retention audit logs we can pull during procurement review?
3) Is there a short-term path to 0-retention for a scoped subset of the data (e.g., metadata-only) if security insists after seeing the demonstrator?

Procurement asks for a simple addendum + an abbreviated SOC2 evidence package before they’ll sign. We can send our standard pilot addendum template — I can drop it to procurement@greenlinehealth.com today.

Samantha Li
Senior Procurement Manager
Greenline Health

Hi Samantha — looping in details on the tech pieces we discussed. Short answers up front: yes, the redaction can run in your VPC (we support Private deployment flow) and we can provide retention audit logs via an access-controlled S3 bucket or API endpoint.

Technical notes:
- VPC/private deployment: we can deploy the redaction pipeline inside a customer-managed subnet. That pipeline will perform token-level PII detection + rule-based scrubbing prior to any persistence.
- Retention enforcement: route-level TTL is enforced by the runtime; we produce signed audit exports that show the config and deletion triggers (timestamps).
- US residency: during the pilot we will pin the storage region to us-west-2 and provide confirmation snapshots of the bucket ACLs.
- Scoped 0-retention path: we can do a metadata-only mode for a subset of calls (no conversational text retained). This requires a small config change and a rollback plan; see attached retention-pilot-config.yaml.

Attachment: retention-pilot-config.yaml — this is a sample of the actual config we'll apply to the triage route for the pilot. It contains the rule toggles: redaction=true, store_text=false (if you choose metadata-only), ttl_days=7.

Operational checklist I recommend to get started:
1) Greenline provision a test VPC peering or short-term access token so we can stage the redactor (or we run the private package in your environment).
2) Procurement sends the addendum template.
3) Legal & security tradecraft review (Ben/Neha) review the SOC2 snapshot + config and sign-off for the pilot.

I’ll be available tomorrow afternoon for a quick demo of the redactor against a synthetic sample.

—Marissa

Samantha / team — quick legal note on the pilot addendum.

We can accommodate the 7-day trial with the following contract guardrails:
- Pilot addendum limited to the triage route (explicitly identified) and automatically expires after 30 days unless both parties agree in writing to extend.
- No change to retention beyond the pilot duration without a signed amendment.
- Redwood will deliver a signed statement of data handling practices for the pilot and provide the SOC2 evidence packet (summary + control mappings).
- For the scoped 0-retention request, we propose a proof-of-concept cadence: Redwood implements metadata-only for a narrow test collection for 7 days; Greenline verifies via audit logs; if satisfied, both parties sign a bounded amendment to expand 0-retention.

If procurement sends its pilot addendum template, our legal team will mark it up and return redlines within 48 hours. If you prefer we start from our standard pilot addendum, I can circulate it today.

Ben Carter
